place.source_title: Old Hardware Store with an upper veranda (Vermilion)

brief: A two-storey pale-blue clapboard store with a projecting upper veranda on posts with a white rail, shop doors under it and a script 'Hardware' sign board. Two photos. Older than 1970: Lake Erie island and harbour-town main streets (the Put-in-Bay model) are 19th-century commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the old hardware store (Vermilion OH, 1880s): a blue clapboard false-front building with a two-storey porch -- an upper veranda with a white balustrade over a sidewalk porch on posts with brick bases -- double doors with X-braced panels, a brick-paved front

why.note: a lake-town store's porch and upper veranda
